run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T07:14:01Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by a real error burst on frontend-proxy's own spans: the error/total span ratio was 0% up to 07:14, rose from 07:17:01, peaked at 8.29% at 07:19:01 and fell back near 0 by 07:26 (reconstructed from traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy"}). The failing frontend-proxy ingress spans are HTTP 504 with 15.0s duration (its 'router frontend egress' spans error=true, http.status_code=0) and HTTP 503, i.e. its upstream, the frontend, was not answering within the Envoy timeout. The frontend is the service with the most error spans (1588.2 increase vs 820.9 for frontend-proxy) and its failing path is GET /api/data -> grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds. In a whole trace at 07:22:42, /api/data took 24.59s, GetAds 24.59s, the ad service's GetAds 22.37s, and ad's flag-evaluation calls (flagd ResolveBoolean) ended DEADLINE_EXCEEDED while flagd's own handler span was 9us - so the ad service, not flagd, was the slow link; frontend also logged gRPC 14 UNAVAILABLE 'connect ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080', which is the ad Service ClusterIP:8080. The ad Deployment (generation 2) rolled at 07:15:21-23: new ReplicaSet ad-785b4464f5, old pod ad-554b849958-w5fhc killed and old ReplicaSet scaled 1->0, new pod created/started 07:15:21/07:15:23. That Deployment defines no readiness, liveness or startup probe and a 50m CPU limit; the new pod logged 'Ad service starting.' only at 07:20:10 and no request lines at all between 07:14:30 and 07:22:00, while normal request logs resume from 07:25:04. So the only serving ad pod was replaced by one that was added to the ad Service endpoints immediately (no probe) although its JVM had not yet opened :8080: ad was refused then extremely slow for ~7 minutes, which timed out the frontend /api/data calls and produced the 504/503 errors on frontend-proxy. The deepest cause the evidence supports is the ad Deployment's rollout of a slow-starting pod behind an unprobed Service endpoint.

claims.text: frontend-proxy produced 427.2 ingress STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans and 393.7 'router frontend egress' STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans in the window (vs 24393.5 / 24426.0 STATUS_CODE_UNSET), so the alert tracks real error spans of frontend-proxy itself.

frontend-proxy's error ratio (100*error/error+unset span rate, 2m window) was 0 before 07:14, jumped to 3.84% at 07:17:01, peaked at 8.29% at 07:19:01, stayed 5-8% until 07:24, was 1.57% at 07:25:01 and ~0-0.2% from 07:26; a 5m-window evaluation at 07:14:01 gave 0.0585%, non-zero.

The frontend-proxy error spans are ingress HTTP 504 with ~15.0s duration (10 spans with duration_us 14999448-15000561) plus HTTP 503s with 0.04-1.0s duration, and every one has a child 'router frontend egress' span with error=true and http.status_code=0, i.e. the failure is in the frontend leg behind frontend-proxy.

By service, error-span increases over the window are frontend 1588.2, frontend-proxy 820.9, recommendation 4.06, ad 1.02, fraud-detection 1.02, accounting 0 and payment 0 - the frontend is the largest error source.

Inside the frontend, the error spans are concentrated on one path: 'GET' 393.46, 'GET /api/data' 393.46, 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' 393.46 and client 'grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' 393.62, while POST /api/checkout, POST /api/cart and CartService/CheckoutService calls show 0 error spans.

Frontend error spans at 07:22:33-07:22:35 are HTTP 500 on GET and GET /api/data whose exception message is '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080' on grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds (rpc.grpc.status_code=14); the message text embeds the timestamp 2025-12-15T17:53:00.348Z, which does not match the span time.

100.70.197.56 is the ClusterIP of the otel-demo 'ad' Service on port 8080 (its only endpoint at query time is pod IP 100.96.3.224:8080), so the ECONNREFUSED errors were frontend calls to the ad Service.

Whole trace d4057d2e24ea083d01006c39cd8fcd6a (start 07:22:42): frontend-proxy egress span 15.000151s -> ingress 504; frontend GET /api/data 24.594s; frontend GetAds client span 24.593s; ad 'oteldemo.AdService/GetAds' 22.372s; inside ad, three 'resolve'->'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean' client spans of 1.600s, 3.600s and 2.299s ended rpc.grpc.status_code=4 (DEADLINE_EXCEEDED), while the flagd server-side span lasted 9us with status description 'context deadline exceeded'.

The ad Deployment is at generation 2 with a Progressing condition lastUpdateTime 07:15:23 ('ReplicaSet "ad-785b4464f5" has successfully progressed') and its ad container has no readinessProbe, livenessProbe or startupProbe and a cpu limit of 50m / memory limit 450Mi; the old ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 and the new ad-785b4464f5 both still exist.

Events show the ad rollout at 07:15:21-07:15:23: 'Killing' and 'SuccessfulDelete' for pod ad-554b849958-w5fhc, 'SuccessfulCreate' for ad-785b4464f5-9bshh, 'Scaled up replica set ad-785b4464f5 from 0 to 1' and 'Scaled down replica set ad-554b849958 from 1 to 0'; no events exist for frontend, frontend-proxy or flagd in the returned set.

The replacement ad pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh was created 07:15:21 with its container started 07:15:23, restartCount 0 and no last termination, yet its log contains 'Ad service starting.' only at 07:20:10.907 and no request lines at all between 07:14:30 and 07:22:00; normal per-request lines ('Targeted ad request received...') appear from 07:25:04 onward.

The flagd pod flagd-5466bf5bc-jfcxr started 06:45:09 with restartCount 0, its Deployment runs with a cpu limit of 250m and generation 2, and its observed spans are fast (9us ResolveBoolean handler; server-side EventStream span with rpc.grpc.status_code=0).

Checked and found without errors tied to this cause: accounting and payment show 0 error spans in the window, and the frontend's checkout/cart operations (POST /api/checkout, POST /api/cart, CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, CartService/GetCart, CartService/AddItem) show 0 error spans; cart spans in a 503 trace completed with rpc.grpc.status_code=0.

fraud-detection changed during the window for another reason: its container was OOMKilled with exit code 137 at 06:49:59 and restarted (restartCount 1, 'Created'/'Started' events at 07:22:11-07:22:12); fraud-detection accounts for only ~1 error span over the whole window.

Root cause: the otel-demo 'ad' Deployment's generation-2 rollout at 07:15:21 replaced its only serving pod (ad-554b849958-w5fhc) with ad-785b4464f5-9bshh, which has no readiness probe and therefore joined the ad Service endpoints immediately although its JVM only opened :8080 around 07:20-07:22. Traffic to ad:8080 was refused (frontend gRPC 14 UNAVAILABLE / ECONNREFUSED 100.70.197.56:8080) and then answered in 20-25s, exceeding frontend-proxy's 15s upstream timeout, which produced the 504/503 errors behind the alert.

Why ad was slow rather than merely absent: the ad container's 50m CPU limit plus JVM cold start starved its request threads - the ad-side flagd client spans lasted 1.6-3.6s while the matching flagd server handler ran in 9us and a 2.6s gap exists between client send and server receipt, and the GetAds span shows ~10.6s of internal delay before the first flag resolution. CPU throttling data was not available to confirm the mechanism.

flagd (otel-demo/flagd) as the bottleneck was considered and rejected: its deployment is generation 2 with a 250m CPU limit and started before this window (pod start 06:45:07-06:45:09, 0 restarts), the errors against it are user-side DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, its ResolveBoolean handler span was 9us and its EventStream server span reported rpc.grpc.status_code=0; the 600s DEADLINE_EXCEEDED /flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream spans seen for recommendation are that client's stream-renewal pattern (only ~4 such error spans in the window) rather than flagd failure.

The fraud-detection OOMKill/restart (exit 137 at 06:49:59, container recreated 07:22:11) was considered as a cause and rejected: the failing frontend path is /api/data -> AdService/GetAds with 393.5 error spans while checkout/cart operations show 0 errors, and fraud-detection contributes only ~1 error span in the window.

Add a readinessProbe (gRPC/TCP on :8080) and/or a startupProbe to the ad container in Deployment otel-demo/ad so a new pod is not added to the ad Service endpoints until its JVM is actually listening; consider a longer rollout settling time or a warm spare for this single-replica, JVM-based service.

Review whether the ad container's cpu limit of 50m (request 10m) is adequate for the JVM, since the observed 20-25s responses and multi-second scheduling gaps in the new pod are consistent with CPU starvation; confirm against container CPU throttling metrics, which were not available in this Run.

Confirm in change history which ad Deployment field changed to produce generation 2 (image vs resources vs other spec) before deciding whether the rollout itself or the pod template's probe/limit settings is the primary defect; that data source is not integrated in this Run.

gaps: The alerting rule RequestErrorRate is not loaded in the queried Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules by name and unfiltered returned no data), so its exact expression and evaluation window are unknown; the annotation's 'current: 2.4555555555555553' could not be reproduced from traces_span_metrics_calls_total (0.0585% at 07:14:01, peak 8.29% at 07:19:01).

kube-state-metrics series (kube_pod_container_info, kube_pod_owner, kube_replicaset_owner, kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready) returned no data in this window, so the endpoint-readiness timeline of the ad Service and the new pod's image digest (image change vs config-only change) could not be verified from metrics.

The frontend pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-x27kw returned no log lines at all in 07:14-07:32 (0 bytes read), so the frontend's own error output could not be inspected; the ad pod's previous container logs are unavailable because the pre-rollout pod ad-554b849958-w5fhc was deleted.
No container CPU throttling/usage metrics were available, so the CPU-starvation explanation for the ad pod's 20-25s responses remains a hypothesis.

The change_history integration is not available, so which field of the ad Deployment changed at generation 2 (and whether the 50m CPU limit or probe configuration was altered by that rollout) cannot be established.
Traces are a biased sample (Jaeger keeps a limited number of traces) and the alert's exact window alignment with the 07:17-07:25 error burst cannot be proven because the rule is missing.
next_steps: Check the ad Deployment's change history to identify what changed at generation 2 (07:15:21) and whether the cpu limit/probes were modified.
Inspect container CPU throttling (container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total) for pod ad-785b4464f5-9bshh if such metrics can be enabled, to confirm or refute CPU starvation.
Verify with the Kubernetes API/history whether the ad Service endpoints contained the new pod before 07:22 (readiness timeline), since kube-state-metrics series were absent.
Add readiness/startup probes to the ad container and re-test a rolling update to confirm the outage no longer reproduces.
